gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2's solar input accepts only 12–28 V, and that its manual warns against any panel whose open-circuit voltage is above 28 V. Two of BLUETTI's own 100 W panels wired in series reach 2 × 24.62 V = 49.24 V, so they are ruled out. A single 200 W BLUETTI panel (24.6 V open-circuit) is the one-panel way to reach the station's 200 W solar maximum.
standout_why: I read the cited rivals solar-home.space, campequipmentplus.com and solutionenergy.com, plus our own current page. solar-home.space gives only maximum watts (Explorer 300 v2 '100 W', RIVER 3 Plus 220 W) and lists the Anker C300X DC kits by name and price only. campequipmentplus.com says it gives no voltage range or connector for any product and says only 'voltage and current limits matter'. solutionenergy.com gives a voltage range only for the Anker C1000 Gen 2 (29–60 V) and a connector only for Jackery (DC8020), and none for the small 300 Wh kits. None of them covers the Elite 30 V2's voltage limit, which panels fit under it, or the rule against wiring two panels in series. Our current page says nothing about any of this either.
decides: It confirms the Elite 30 V2 + 100 W kit as the pick and adds a limit to its upgrade path. A shopper can go up to the 200 W solar maximum in two ways: one BLUETTI 200 W panel (24.6 V open-circuit), or 100 W panels wired in parallel. Two 100 W panels wired in series exceed the 28 V limit. BLUETTI also says the station does not support an expansion battery. So for longer trips the upgrade is the AC180, not more storage for the Elite 30 V2.
candidates: Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 (Explorer 1000 v2 + SolarSaga 200 W)

findings.label: Solar input voltage range and open-circuit voltage ceiling
findings.value: 12–28 V; do not use panels with an open-circuit voltage above 28 V
findings.source_title: BLUETTI ELITE 30 V2 Portable Power Station 600W – User Manual V3.0 (manualsfile mirror)
findings.note: Quotes from the manual: 'Solar input voltage range for the unit is 12V-28V.' and 'Do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 28V.' This is a mirror of BLUETTI's manual. BLUETTI's own copy (V1.0, https://s4.bluettipower.com/bluetti_lgf/support/2025/08/3310400e-57e7-4b62-b1fc-030bd780a06e.pdf, linked from support.bluettipower.com) downloaded, but I couldn't extract its text to check it.

findings.label: Kit price and stock at BLUETTI US
findings.note: Checked with storecheck.py (Shopify product JSON). The 60 W kit is $399.99 and the station alone is $289.99, both from the same store search. The in-the-box list on the product page doesn't name the panel model or the solar cable.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage, Isc, connector, series/parallel rule
findings.value: Voc 24.62 V; Isc 5.13 A; MC4; can be wired in series or parallel only with PV100L/PV100D; BLUETTI advises against mixing other brands or panel types
findings.note: Arithmetic: two SP100L in series = 2 × 24.62 V = 49.24 V, which is above the Elite 30 V2's 28 V ceiling. In parallel the voltage stays at 24.62 V and Isc adds to 10.26 A. The SP100L page doesn't name the Elite 30 V2. It says the panel is 'compatible with all BLUETTI portable power stations'. Store price is $249.

findings.label: Open-circuit voltage, Isc, connector, mixing rule
findings.value: Voc 24.6 V; Isc 10.8 A; MC4; BLUETTI does not encourage mixing panel models (for example PV200 with SP200L)
findings.note: 24.6 V is below the Elite 30 V2's 28 V limit, so one SP200L fits the voltage window and matches the 200 W maximum. The page also gives conflicting ship dates ('late July' and 'from November 18th'). Store price is $399.
